claims.text: Tungsten and molybdenum are refractory-element candidates for the proposed intervention.
Adding tungsten or molybdenum to a high-entropy nanoalloy can improve its high-temperature structural stability relative to an otherwise comparable alloy without the addition.
Adding tungsten or molybdenum to a high-entropy nanoalloy can improve its high-temperature chemical stability relative to an otherwise comparable alloy without the addition.
The proposed benefit is expected under high-temperature application conditions.
Introducing the refractory element can form a stable solid solution.
Introducing the refractory element can produce a chemically homogeneous phase.
The refractory-element addition reduces diffusion rates in the alloy.
The refractory-element addition increases the activation energy of degradation processes.
Reduced diffusion rates improve the high-temperature stability of the alloy.
A higher activation energy for degradation improves the high-temperature stability of the alloy.
Improved structural and chemical stability will enhance high-temperature performance.
Improved structural and chemical stability will increase service longevity at high temperature.
The refractory-element concentration must remain within a composition window to avoid unwanted phases or precipitation.
The optimal refractory-element composition and processing conditions are unknown.
Formation of unwanted phases or precipitates after refractory-element addition is proposed as evidence that the hypothesis is falsified.
